meta.description: Infers ligand-receptor cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq with a consensus-first workflow (LIANA), plus CellPhoneDB specificity tests, CellChat pathway probabilities, and NicheNet downstream ligand-activity. Use when ranking ligand-receptor interactions between cell types, comparing communication across conditions, asking which ligand drives a receiver response, or deciding which CCC method and resource to trust.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOIs, PMIDs, statistics, or biology anywhere in the fixed SKILL.md or in this re-audit's own real-data outputs (930 resource-robust pairs, CellPhoneDB significant pairs all correspond to real, named receptor-ligand biology: HLA-E/F-VSIR/LILRB1 checkpoints, ICAM2/3-LFA1, CD47-SIRPG, GAS6-MERTK).

practice_boundaries.detail: Still purely basic-research scRNA-seq analysis; no individual-patient diagnostic or prescriptive claims. Unchanged from the pre-fix audit.

methodological_ground.detail: Governing Principle and Confounds table remain intact and correct. The new Condition Comparison section correctly avoids comparing raw counts and hedges gained/lost pairs as 'candidates', not proof -- it does not teach a fallacy. It does, however, omit a baseline-noise caveat (see P1 recommendation): a re-auditor-constructed null-case split with no true biological difference still produced 271/981 (27.6%) 'gained or lost' calls from sampling noise alone. This is a completeness gap, not an active methodological fallacy, so it does not meet the M3 FAIL bar.

code_usability.detail: All executable code paths (LIANA consensus, LIANA resource-sensitivity, CellPhoneDB guarded specificity, Condition Comparison) ran to completion on real PBMC 1k v3 data in fresh, independent re-auditor runs with zero crashes. CellPhoneDB's documented debug_seed=1337 call is runnable and mostly but not fully deterministic at the documented threads=4 (see P1) -- a reliability defect, not an 'unrunnable code' defect, so it does not meet the M4 FAIL bar. CellChat/NicheNet remain out of live-execution scope on this Windows box (unchanged, GitHub-only packages per TOOLS.md); not touched by this fix, verified by git diff.

functional_suitability.note: Both original factual inaccuracies are now fixed and independently re-verified (single-group ValueError text matches the real exception; CellPhoneDB no longer crashes on Windows). Offsetting this, the Permutation Rationale table's debug_seed claim ('set it explicitly for reproducible reporting') is not fully accurate for the documented threads=4 call -- re-verified: 82/120,375 significance flags still flip across two fresh runs at the exact shipped parameters.

reliability.note: The __main__ guard and its rationale are now documented inline. No proactive warning that reproducibility depends on threads=1, and no structured SKILL_* error codes for the agent-first context -- unchanged from the pre-fix audit.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md grew from 221 to 270 lines (new Prerequisites and Condition Comparison sections) but remains well within a manageable budget; still loads all five methods' code eagerly rather than layering into references/.

agent_usability.note: Method Decision Table and terminology remain unambiguous and fully consistent; unaffected by the fix.

human_usability.note: usage-guide.md is now leaner (redundant sections removed) without losing Example Prompts; unaffected in substance.

security.note: Unchanged: no credentials, no raw-string execution, no injection vectors.

maintainability.note: Still only 2 of 5 documented methods (LIANA, CellChat) have a matching examples/ script; CellPhoneDB, NicheNet, and the new Condition Comparison section exist only as inline SKILL.md code.

inputs.label: CellPhoneDB v5 guarded, seeded specificity test -- fresh independent dual-run determinism check
inputs.note: Ran SKILL.md's now-guarded, now-seeded (debug_seed=1337) 'Specificity Test' block twice, independently, exactly as documented (threshold=0.1, iterations=1000, threads=4, score_interactions=True). Crash is genuinely fixed: both fresh runs completed with no RuntimeError. Determinism is NOT fully fixed at the documented threads=4: comparing the FULL pvalues matrix (120,375 cell-pair x interaction values, not a spot check) across the two fresh runs found 5,150 differing cells (max abs diff 0.075) and 82/120,375 flipped significance flags at p<0.05 -- down from the pre-fix audit's 252/120,375, but not the 0/120,375 the fix log and SKILL.md's own Permutation Rationale table claim. A follow-up isolation run at threads=1 (the fixer's actual verification setting, per the fix commit message) reproduced the fix log's claim exactly: 0/120,375 differing cells, fully bit-identical. The non-determinism is specific to the threads=4 multiprocessing path that SKILL.md actually documents.

inputs.label: Compare CCC between two conditions using the new Condition Comparison section -- re-auditor's own null-case split
inputs.note: The fixer's own verification used an arbitrary 50/50 split with no stated rationale. To test whether the new section actually protects against spurious differences (its stated purpose), the re-auditor built an independent, stratified-by-cell_type random split (different RNG seed, 20260919) that preserves per-cell-type composition and, by construction, has NO true biological difference between 'conditionA' and 'conditionB'. The code ran end-to-end with zero errors (555 vs 558 cells, 827 vs 864 robust pairs). Finding: even under this true null, 154 gained + 117 lost pairs out of 981 union robust pairs (27.6%) were flagged purely from sampling noise and the halved per-condition cell count -- comparable in scale to the fixer's own demo (409 gained/70 lost). SKILL.md gives no warning that a similar fraction of any real two-condition gained/lost call may be noise, and recommends no stability check (e.g. repeat-split or bootstrap).

recommendations.title: CellPhoneDB determinism fix is verified only at threads=1, but SKILL.md documents threads=4
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's shipped 'Specificity Test' code block uses threads=4 with debug_seed=1337. Two fresh, independent re-audit runs at those exact parameters differed on 5,150/120,375 p-values and flipped 82/120,375 significance flags. The Permutation Rationale table's claim ('set it explicitly for reproducible reporting') is not accurate for the code block directly above it. A threads=1 run with the same seed is fully bit-identical (0/120,375 differ) -- this is what the fix log and commit message actually verified, per their own stated iterations=100, threads=1 parameters.
recommendations.root_cause: cellphonedb's multiprocessing.Pool-based permutation workers do not deterministically replay the RNG stream across worker counts even with debug_seed fixed; the fixer's verification used a thread count the shipped code does not use.
recommendations.fix: Either change the documented call to threads=1 for reproducible reporting (accept ~3-5x slower runtime on datasets this size), or add an explicit caveat to the Permutation Rationale table: 'debug_seed is bit-reproducible at threads=1; at threads>1, marginal (near p=0.05) calls may still flip run-to-run.'

recommendations.title: Condition Comparison section has no baseline sampling-noise warning
recommendations.problem: A re-auditor-constructed null-case split (stratified random, no true biological difference, different seed than the fixer's) still produced a 27.6% gained/lost fraction of the robust-pair union from sampling noise and halved per-condition cell counts alone. SKILL.md gives no guidance that a comparable fraction of any real two-condition comparison's gained/lost pairs may be noise, and recommends no stability check.
recommendations.root_cause: The new section was validated by confirming it runs and produces plausible counts, not by checking its behavior under a known-null comparison.
recommendations.fix: Add a caveat recommending a repeat-split or bootstrap stability check (e.g., re-run the split N times and report each pair's gained/lost frequency) before treating a single split's gained/lost set as a finding, mirroring the rigor of the existing Resource-Sensitivity Check.
